title: AirSTAR: A UAV Platform for Flight Dynamics and Control System Testing
relevance: Primary platform description for AirSTAR: a 5.5% dynamically scaled twin-turbine generic transport with about a 7 ft span, more than 70 downlink channels, and telemetry above 200 Hz. It establishes the scale and instrumentation context for the T-2/GTM flight-identification and high-angle-of-attack papers in this collection.
limitations: This is a research-facility and vehicle overview, not a hobby sport-jet dataset or a complete aerodynamic coefficient publication. Its dynamic-similarity claims apply to the documented test configuration and should not be transferred to ordinary RC models.

title: Practical Application of a Subscale Transport Aircraft for Flight Research in Control Upset and Failure Conditions
relevance: The S-2 is a COTS subscale transport surrogate, about 7.083 ft span and 1.502 slugs full-fuel mass, with one aft-mounted JetCat P120SE. The authors report ground static-thrust and throttle-step measurements, identify an RPM/thrust first-order response whose time constant varies from 0.85 to 1.96 s (faster above half power), infer ram drag from flight acceleration, and compare an independently withheld yaw-roll doublet at about 80 kt against simulation.
limitations: S-2 is a NASA-instrumented transport surrogate with similar size and wing loading to the dynamically scaled research aircraft, not a sport jet and not the same vehicle as T-2/GTM. The demonstrated simulation prediction is near the middle of the envelope; the paper says near-stall prediction remained future work. The measured P120SE behavior is installation- and test-specific.

title: Flight Test Maneuvers for Efficient Aerodynamic Modeling
relevance: Demonstrates optimized orthogonal multisine surface inputs on a subscale jet transport to excite all six rigid-body degrees of freedom near selected trim conditions, with real-time and post-flight frequency-domain equation-error modeling. limitations: This NASA AirSTAR experiment is a twin-turbine, dynamically scaled transport, not a sport jet. The method requires suitable instrumentation and a flight-control/augmentation setup; its maneuver results do not supply universal RC coefficients.

title: Aerodynamic Parameter Estimation Using Reconstructed Turbulence Measurements
relevance: Uses a subscale transport-type airplane’s flight data in moderate and severe turbulence to estimate longitudinal short-period stability/control derivatives. Reconstructed vertical gust measurements reduce regressor correlation and allow pitch-rate and angle-of-attack-rate terms to be identified in straight-and-level flight without special excitation maneuvers.
limitations: NTRS identifies this item as a preprint, not a final journal version. It is an estimator result from a particular instrumented subscale transport, not a hobby model or a publicly downloadable telemetry dataset.

title: A Method for Improved Flight Testing of Remotely Piloted Aircraft Using Multisine Inputs
relevance: Reports simulation and actual subscale flight tests using ground-based flight-control augmentation to inject low-correlated multisines and an instrumental-variable frequency-domain method. The test aircraft is the same GFF platform described in the 2016 ICAS report, so this adds a distinct identification campaign/method rather than a second airframe.
limitations: Focused on initial envelope expansion and linear-regression identification under near-ground, short-pass RPA constraints; this is not a high-alpha or post-stall dataset. The GFF’s stable forward-CG configuration and local atmospheric conditions bound transfer of its results.

title: Experimental and Theoretical Assessment of Aerodynamic and Stability Derivatives of a Subscale Aircraft
relevance: Uses a 3D-printed 1/2-scale model of the BAe Hawk D006 aeromodel (half of the RC model, not half of a full-size Hawk) for wind-tunnel measurements of static lift/drag and lateral-directional derivatives and comparison with AVL/VLM estimates. limitations: This is a tunnel and computational study, not free-flight or turbine/EDF validation. It reports static derivatives only; the paper says dynamic flight data were future work. The lift/drag coefficients vary with tunnel speed, and lateral testing could not reach the scaled stall speed.
